To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the predictive power of software quality models derived from static product measures is very low.

(a) no predictive model is better than another; (b) the best model achieves 70% of the achieved quality of the best human tester; (c) the achieved quality of any model is 30-50% of the achieved human quality; and (d) the verification cost of any model is about 50% of the verification cost of a human tester.

(a) none of the models we tested was able to effectively classify components as low-risk or high-risk; (b) the models that performed best were those that used a combination of measures and those that used a large number of measures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of predictive models that are derived from software measures.
the problem of building quality models from software measures and with the problem of evaluating the predictive quality models that are derived.
the development of a methodology that allows the prediction of the quality of software systems, based on software product measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modeling techniques we evaluated are not yet able to provide the quality assurance community with a reliable and accurate tool for predicting software faults.
the models evaluated in this study are not yet mature enough for practical use.
the predictive models were not able to predict the quality of software with a reasonable degree of accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of a software component cannot be predicted with the available measures.

, while we were able to develop models that can predict with high accuracy the quality of a software product, we were unable to build models that can predict whether a software component will be faulty or not.

, although the predictive models are not effective in discriminating between faulty and fault-free components, the modeling techniques are effective in identifying the most important measures for the prediction of software quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of the data used in the modeling is critical to the success of any predictive model.
it is not possible to predict the quality of software products using the measures we have considered in this study.
the quality of software is not predictable based solely on the analysis of the product.
